defect_reproduced.root_cause: CallbackBridge._process_batch treated every BusyThreadError (including ActiveThreadSteerDeferralError/SidebandUnavailableError) identically to a genuine AppServerError: both shared the same batch.attempts counter and both dead-lettered once attempts >= DEFAULT_MAX_RETRIES=5. A temporary active/busy Codex thread therefore exhausted the SAME bounded failure budget meant for real transport/protocol failures. _process_batch also blocked the whole poll loop with an in-process time.sleep(retry_delay) (up to DEFAULT_RETRY_BACKOFF_MAX=300s) before each retried delivery attempt, so one busy thread could stall processing of every other thread's due work.

changes: AITools/taskdb.py: callback_batches gains three idempotently-migrated columns -- not_before_at (earliest re-claim time; empty = due now), hard_failure_count (the bounded dead-letter budget for GENUINE failures only), last_failure_kind ('busy'|'transient_error'|'', redacted-safe signal for status).

AITools/taskdb.py: new defer_batch_busy(conn, batch_id, error, delay_seconds=...) -- returns a busy-deferred batch to pending with a scheduled not_before_at, NEVER touches hard_failure_count, NEVER dead-letters, however many times called.

AITools/taskdb.py: new fail_batch_transient(conn, batch_id, error, max_retries=, delay_seconds=...) -- the genuine-failure path: increments hard_failure_count and either reschedules (non-blockingly, via not_before_at) or dead-letters once hard_failure_count reaches max_retries. Returns 'requeued'|'dead_letter'.

AITools/taskdb.py: requeue_batch() removed -- its two call sites (busy vs genuine failure) were exactly the bug (one shared bounded-retry path for both); replaced by the two functions above with independent counters.

AITools/taskdb.py: claim_pending_callback_batch() now skips a 'pending' batch whose not_before_at is still in the future (continues scanning other candidates instead of returning it) and reserves a thread with ANY non-terminal batch (pending OR inflight, due or not) from new-batch formation, so a not-yet-due busy park can never be split into a second competing batch for the same thread.
AITools/taskdb.py: _reclaim_expired_batches() clears not_before_at on lease-expiry (crash/restart) recovery -- a crashed bridge process is never held back by a stale busy-backoff schedule.

AITools/taskdb.py: callback_batch_stats() gains waiting_for_thread_idle_batch_count (pending, last_failure_kind='busy') and pending_genuine_failure_batch_count (pending, last_failure_kind='transient_error') -- redacted-safe, no origin_thread_id or payload text.

callback_bridge.py::CallbackBridge._process_batch: removed the in-process time.sleep(retry_delay) blocking wait entirely. BusyThreadError (ActiveThreadSteerDeferralError/SidebandThreadBusyError) calls defer_batch_busy with computed non-blocking backoff; SidebandUnavailableError and every other infrastructure AppServerError call fail_batch_transient and retain bounded dead-letter at five genuine failures.
implementation.exception_ordering_preserved: BusyThreadError is checked before AppServerError, so ActiveThreadSteerDeferralError/SidebandThreadBusyError park durably. SidebandUnavailableError is an AppServerError rather than BusyThreadError and therefore uses the bounded genuine-failure route.
implementation.second_turn_never_started: select_steer_target/turn/steer/turn/start logic (B407/B409) is unchanged -- this task only changes what happens to the durable outbox/batch record AFTER a deferral or failure is raised, never the App Server RPC sequence itself.
implementation.no_regex_or_table_cognition: Pure deterministic queue/lease bookkeeping (SQL state transitions on callback_batches/callback_outbox) -- no learned decision, no keyword/cue router; N/A to the neural-control-first doctrine.
